pr_body:
This commit fixes the UseDx mode for conhost.
In order to add support for UseDx without calling `SetWindowSize`,
responsibility for resizing `_invalidMap` has been moved to occur
only when the renderer itself recognizes a new size. Furthermore
`InvalidateAll` is now the central point to invalidate `_invalidMap`.

## Validation Steps Performed

* Enabling `UseDx` enables the DxEngine for conhost ✔️
* Resizing windows in conhost works ✔️
* Resizing windows in WT works ✔️

Closes #5455
pr_comments: Make sure you test unusual scenarios too, like doing a *lot*  of resizing in WT, with multiple panes, and moving between displays of different DPIs (or changing your active DPI)

issue_context.title: Conhost output is invisible when UseDx is set
issue_context.body:
# Environment

Windows build number: Version 10.0.18362.657
Windows Terminal version (if applicable): Commit f6f0731eae61f24e6777e5cf98aaf7e746f1b2bd

# Steps to reproduce

1. Set the DWORD registry value `HKCU\Console\UseDx` to `1` to enable the DirectX renderer.
2. Build the latest source (or at least commit 79684bf82177dfa52bd1eca84476a2950d765bb9).
3. Start a cmd shell in conhost (the problem isn't exclusive to the cmd shell though).

# Expected behavior

I'd expect to see the copyright message and command prompt.

# Actual behavior

The screen is blank. I can still see the cursor, but any text output is invisible. It's like it's rendering everything in black on black.

This was working for me in commit ffbdfe32ac972ecf76ead140a2ae5bad59cf6f91, but broke after commit 79684bf82177dfa52bd1eca84476a2950d765bb9. It still seems to be broken in the latest commit (f6f0731eae61f24e6777e5cf98aaf7e746f1b2bd).
comments: Thanks for filing this one. We quasi-knowingly broke conhost with that PR :/

(`UseDx` used to be hidden behind Windows' feature gating infrastructure, so it was only really _incidentally_ available because we stripped that stuff out going open-source. It's not "supported", but we try not to break things like that generally.)
I figured it might have been something like that. Not a big deal. Just wanted to make sure you were aware of the issue.

review_comments: Due to the missing `std::min`, but the delayed `_invalidMap` resize, this was blowing up with exceptions. Now it isn't anymore.

I'm sure @miniksa will agree:

i am surprised we do not have `til::rectangle::clamp`
I mean we do technically have an `operator&`, but I found it cumbersome to first construct a rectangle (which is rather verbose) just to do `& rc`.
I personally prefer Dustin's, but I'll take either. The structures and operators are tools to make life easier... not a strict requirement.
If I'm reading this correctly, there isn't a strong opinion... as I'd like to keep it the way I did it for now, if you don't mind. 😅

I'm confused -- the body of the PR says "responsibility for resizing `_invalidMap` has been moved entirely into `InvalidateAll`", but both places we have InvalidateAll calls we resize the map _before_ calling it?
Woops I mixed things up. I'm fixing my PR body to say that responsibility for full invalidation was moved there.

Why did you pull this? I presume the answer is:
1. No one ever set this so we'll always just invalidate a full row.
2. We determined that we likely won't even need to do differential drawing with a better render strategy anyway so there's no reason to try to tighten down the differential drawing any further in the future by doing partial rows.
If that's the answer... maybe leave some of that in a comment in `InvalidateRectangle` so we don't forget.

Yeah basically that. I was touching the only function that uses this field and I doubt this field will ever be useful again, as it's slower to figure out what contains ligatures, compared to just redrawing the entire row. The difference between drawing no text and a full row of text is only ~5μs after all. (Also: YAGNI. 😄)
